subject: Problem with simple linux plotting with qplot

messages.author: 28a0214e419a864f
messages.subject: Problem with simple linux plotting with qplot
parts:
I apologize if I'm missing something really obvious here, but a
function that used to give me no problems is now giving me the error:
"Error in function (d, p) : argument "p" is missing, with no default."
I thought it was my code, but it's not working with the simple example
from the help page. All of this code works in R 2.10 on my mac, but is
suddenly not working on our linux system.

> qplot(1:10, letters[1:10])
Error in function (d, p) : argument "p" is missing, with no default

> qplot(1:10, rnorm(10), colour = runif(10))
Error in function (d, p) : argument "p" is missing, with no default
>

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.9.0 (2009-04-17)
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

locale:
LC_CTYPE=C;LC_NUMERIC=C;LC_TIME=C;LC_COLLATE=C;LC_MONETARY=C;LC_MESSAGES=en_US.
$

[1] grid stats graphics grDevices utils datasets
methods
[8] base

[1] ggplot2_0.8.8 proto_0.3-8 reshape_0.8.3 plyr_1.2.1

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):

Any help would be appreciated, and thanks!

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Problem with simple linux plotting with qplot
parts:
Hi:

Works for me on 64-bit R, Win 7, R 2.11.1. Try it again in a fresh R session to see if that helps. If not, wait until tomorrow and upgrade to 2.12.0 :)  Perhaps you have an object p in your workspace that creates a clash with qplot?

Dennis
